---
title: "Multi-sample and cross-source integration"
description: "How to QC, merge, integrate, validate, and model biological multi-sample studies and cross-dataset SCOP objects."
---

Two situations look similar in code but support different conclusions.

## Biological multi-sample design {#biological-multi-sample-design}

Use this path when `sample_id` identifies independent donors, animals, or experimental units.

```r
objects <- SplitObject(merged, split.by = "sample_id")

objects <- lapply(objects, function(x) {
  x[["percent.mt"]] <- PercentageFeatureSet(x, pattern = "^MT-")
  RunCellQC(
    x,
    assay = "RNA",
    qc_metrics = c("umi", "gene", "mito", "outlier"),
    return_filtered = FALSE
  )
})
```

Inspect distributions and retention by sample. A sample that loses 80% of cells is a study-level warning, not merely a cell-filtering detail.

After recorded filtering and doublet calling:

```r
srt <- merge(objects[[1]], y = objects[-1], add.cell.ids = names(objects))
srt <- JoinLayers(srt)
srt <- SCTransform(srt, assay = "RNA", vst.flavor = "v2", verbose = FALSE)
```

Only integrate when batch/source variation is unwanted and not confounded with the biological contrast:

```r
srt <- Harmony_integrate(
  srt_merge = srt,
  batch = "batch",
  assay = "SCT",
  normalization_method = "SCT",
  do_normalization = FALSE,
  HVF = VariableFeatures(srt),
  linear_reduction_dims_use = 1:20,
  harmony_dims_use = 1:20,
  seed = 20260807
)
```

## Cross-source integration {#cross-source-integration}

The executed case uses `panc8_sub`: 1,600 pancreatic cells, exactly 200 from each of eight public dataset sources spanning five technologies.

```r
data(panc8_sub, package = "scop")
srt <- JoinLayers(panc8_sub)
srt <- SCTransform(
  srt, assay = "RNA", new.assay.name = "SCT",
  vst.flavor = "v2", variable.features.n = 2000,
  verbose = FALSE
)

srt <- Harmony_integrate(
  srt_merge = srt,
  batch = "dataset",
  assay = "SCT",
  normalization_method = "SCT",
  do_normalization = FALSE,
  do_HVF_finding = FALSE,
  HVF = VariableFeatures(srt),
  do_scaling = FALSE,
  linear_reduction_dims = 30,
  linear_reduction_dims_use = 1:20,
  harmony_dims_use = 1:20,
  cluster_resolution = 0.4,
  seed = 20260807
)
```

![Real panc8 cells before and after Harmony.](assets/figures/real-data/cross-source-integration.png){fig-alt="Three panels compare source separation before Harmony, source mixing after Harmony, and cell-type structure after Harmony."}

## Validate both removal and preservation

Using each cell’s 20 nearest neighbours:

| Metric | Before | After |
|---|---:|---:|
| neighbours from another source | 0.2169 | **0.6765** |
| neighbours with the same known cell type | 0.9379 | **0.9616** |

The cluster-majority label agrees with the bundled cell type for **96.81%** of cells. Together, these checks show improved technical-source mixing without loss of the known cell-type structure in this example.

## Multi-dataset merge decision

| Situation | Recommended action |
|---|---|
| Same features, same technology, separate samples | read separately, per-sample QC, merge, then decide whether integration is needed |
| Same tissue, different technologies | standardise feature identifiers, keep `dataset`/`tech`, integrate and validate |
| Different tissues or incompatible biology | do not force a joint atlas; analyse separately or map to a common reference |
| Condition completely confounded with batch | no integration method can recover the missing design; stop or narrow the claim |
| Reference + new query | use label transfer; do not merge merely to transfer names |

## Differential analysis after integration

Use the integrated reduction for neighbourhoods and visualisation, but return to raw counts for pseudobulk:

```r
counts <- GetAssayData(srt, assay = "RNA", layer = "counts")
# aggregate counts by sample_id × cell_type
# model condition with edgeR/DESeq2 using biological samples
```

Never use the number of cells as the replicate count for a patient-level contrast.

::: {.boundary}
The eight `panc8_sub` sources are technical datasets, not eight patients. They validate integration and cell-type signal. They cannot support population-level inference.
:::
